html:
Madugandí is a Guna comarca, a self-governed Indigenous territory, in the upper Bayano River valley east of Panama City. The Guna are a Chibchan-speaking people best known from the islands and coast of Guna Yala on the Caribbean side of Panama.

In the 1500s the Guna lived further east, in the forests of Darién and Urabá, and moved toward the coasts and the Bayano in later centuries, partly to escape Spanish pressure. They farmed, hunted and fished in the forest.

In 1976 the Bayano Dam flooded much of the Guna land in the valley, and several villages had to move. After years of protest, Panama created the Comarca Kuna de Madugandí in 1996. Their neighbours include the Emberá. See also Guna.
